newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CBANK SAYS NO REFINANCING REPO ON MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CBANK SAYS NO REFINANCING REPO ON MONDAY.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it would not hold any refinancing repo tenders on Monday as the local banking sector showed sufficient liquidity.
The NBS also said it planned to drain some excess liquidity from the interbank market by selling treasury bills from its portfolio.
"The liquidity situation on the market allowed us to decide as we decided," said Peter Andresic, head of the NBS Open Market Operation Department.
The NBS said it had slated some 500 million crown worth of T-bills bills for sale on Monday. The T-bills on offer will mature in 59 days.
The NBS concludes individual deals with banks when draining liquidity through sales of state securities from its portfolio and it does not disclose rates agreed at these deals.
The central bank monitors market liquidity daily and decides each morning whether to hold any open market operations.
The fulfilment of minimum reserves requirement by commercial banks is one of the NBS's main yardsticks for assessing money market liquidity.
According to NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector, as of August 10, exceeded by 2.81 percent the cumulative volume of funds needed to meet minimum reserves requirements later this month.
The daily volume of minimum reserves for commercial banks totals 36.817 billion crowns in the current reserves period ending August 15.

"Some two billion crowns will leave the market today and even if we sell the planned volume of T-bills from our portfolio, the market will close above 100 percent (of the minimum reserves requirement) on Monday," Andresic said.

The latest NBS repo operation was a one-week refinancing repo tender on Wednesday when the central bank added 2.0 billion crowns at an average rate of 18.17 percent, down from 18.32 percent in similar repo on Tuesday.
